# ============================================================================
# Bootstrap: insert markers into target files
# ============================================================================

# Anchor patterns: section_name|start_regex|end_regex
readonly -a ANCHORS=(
  "process_compliance_never|^### NEVER Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "process_compliance_always|^### ALWAYS Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|^### Task Tracking Hierarchy$|^$|^---$"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|^## Pre-Implementation Checklist$|^## |^---$"
  "autonomous_agent_constraints|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_ANCHOR|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_END"
  "simstim_constraints|SIMSTIM_SKILL_ANCHOR|SIMSTIM_SKILL_END"
  "implementing_tasks_constraints|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_ANCHOR|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_END"
)

bootstrap_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    verbose "Section ${section} already has markers in ${file}, skipping bootstrap"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find anchor for this section
  local anchor_start="" anchor_end=""
  for anchor in "${ANCHORS[@]}"; do
    local a_section a_start a_end
    IFS='|' read -r a_section a_start a_end <<< "$anchor"
    if [[ "$a_section" == "$section" ]]; then
      anchor_start="$a_start"
      anchor_end="$a_end"
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ -z "$anchor_start" ]]; then
    log "WARNING: No anchor defined for section ${section}, skipping"
    return 0
  fi

  # For skill-md sections, use <constraints> tags
  if [[ "$anchor_start" == *"SKILL_ANCHOR"* ]]; then
    verbose "Skill section ${section}: markers will be inserted inside <constraints> block during generation"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find the anchor line and insert markers after the table header
  local matches
  matches=$(grep -c "$anchor_start" "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [[ "$matches" -ne 1 ]]; then
    log "ERROR: Anchor '${anchor_start}' matches ${matches} times in ${file} (expected 1)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Find the section: locate header, keep table header+separator, wrap data rows with markers
  local tmp="${file}.bootstrap-tmp"
  local end_pat1="${anchor_end%%|*}"
  local end_pat2="${anchor_end#*|}"
  awk -v anchor="$anchor_start" \
      -v end_pat1="$end_pat1" \
      -v end_pat2="$end_pat2" \
      -v start_m="$start_marker" \
      -v warning_m="$warning" \
      -v end_m="$end_marker" \
      -v content_m="$content" \
      '
      BEGIN { state="looking"; sep_seen=0 }
      state == "looking" && $0 ~ anchor {
        print; state="in_header"; next
      }
      state == "in_header" {
        # Print everything until we see the separator row (|---|)
        print
        if ($0 ~ /^\|[-|: ]+\|$/) {
          sep_seen=1
          print start_m
          print warning_m
          printf "%s\n", content_m
          state="skipping"
        }
        next
      }
      state == "skipping" {
        if ($0 ~ end_pat1 || $0 ~ end_pat2) {
          print end_m
          if ($0 !~ /^$/) print
          state="done"
          next
        }
        # Skip original data rows (replaced by generated content)
        next
      }
      state != "skipping" { print }
      END {
        if (state == "skipping") print end_m
      }
      ' "$file" > "$tmp"

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    diff -u "$file" "$tmp" || true
    rm -f "$tmp"
  else
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    log "Bootstrapped markers for section '${section}' in ${file}"
  fi
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
     4	#
     5	# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
     6	# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
     7	# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
     8	# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
     9	# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
    10	# =============================================================================
    11	
    12	setup() {
    13	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    14	    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
    15	    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
    16	    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
    17	    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
    18	    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
    19	    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    20	    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    21	}
    22	
    23	# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
    24	# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
    25	add_team_block() {
    26	    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
    27	import sys
    28	p = sys.argv[1]
    29	s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
    30	anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
    31	block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
    32	         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
    33	         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
    34	         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
    35	         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
    36	assert s.count(anchor) == 1
    37	open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
    38	PY
    39	}
    40	
    41	add_team_row() {
    42	    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
    43	        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
    44	        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
    45	        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
    46	    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    47	}
    48

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# validate-constraints.sh — DRY Constraint Registry validator
# Runs 8 validation checks against constraints.json + generated sections
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/compat-lib.sh"

# Constants
readonly REGISTRY=".claude/data/constraints.json"
readonly SCHEMA=".claude/schemas/constraints.schema.json"
readonly TEMPLATE_DIR=".claude/templates/constraints"
readonly GENERATE_SCRIPT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/generate-constraints.sh"

# Section definitions (duplicated from generate-constraints.sh for freshness check)
readonly -a SECTIONS=(
  "process_compliance_never|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"process_compliance_never\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "process_compliance_always|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"process_compliance_always\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|task-tracking.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"task_tracking_hierarchy\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|.claude/protocols/implementation-compliance.md|protocol-checklist.jq|[\"C-PROC-008\",\"C-PROC-006\",\"C-PROC-009\",\"C-PROC-010\",\"C-GIT-001\",\"C-PROC-005\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "deploying_infrastructure_merge|.claude/skills/deploying-infrastructure/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-MERGE-003\",\"C-MERGE-004\",\"C-MERGE-005\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
)

# Counters
ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0
VERBOSE=false

# ============================================================================
# Utilities
# ============================================================================

log() { echo "[validate-constraints] $*" >&2; }
verbose() { [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && log "$@" || true; }
pass() { echo "  PASS: $*"; }
fail() { echo "  FAIL: $*"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }
warn() { echo "  WARN: $*"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1)); }

compute_section_hash() {
  printf '%s' "$1" \
    | tr -d '\r' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' \
    | sha256_portable \
    | cut -c1-16
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 1: Registry exists and is valid JSON
# ============================================================================

check_registry_exists() {
  log "Check 1: Registry exists and is valid JSON"

  if [[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]]; then
    fail "Registry not found: $REGISTRY"
    return 1
  fi

  if ! jq empty "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null; then
    fail "Registry is not valid JSON: $REGISTRY"
    return 1
  fi

  local count
  count=$(jq '.constraints | length' "$REGISTRY")
  pass "Registry is valid JSON with $count constraints"
  return 0
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 2: Schema compliance (ajv or jq fallback)
# ============================================================================

check_schema_compliance() {
  log "Check 2: Schema compliance"

  if [[ ! -f "$SCHEMA" ]]; then
    fail "Schema not found: $SCHEMA"
    return 1
  fi

  if command -v ajv &>/dev/null; then
    if ajv validate -s "$SCHEMA" -d "$REGISTRY" --spec=draft2020 2>&1; then
      pass "Schema validation passed (ajv)"
      return 0
    else
      fail "Schema validation failed (ajv)"
      return 1
    fi
  fi

  # jq fallback: check required fields, ID patterns, enums
  local errors=0

  # Check top-level required fields
  if ! jq -e '.version and .constraints' "$REGISTRY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "Missing required top-level fields (version, constraints)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Check version pattern
  local version
  version=$(jq -r '.version' "$REGISTRY")
  if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    fail "Invalid version format: $version"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check each constraint has required fields
  local missing
  missing=$(jq -r '
    [.constraints[] | select(
      (.id | not) or (.name | not) or (.category | not) or
      (.rule_type | not) or (.text | not) or (.why | not) or
      (.layers | not) or (.severity | not)
    ) | .id // "UNKNOWN"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
    fail "Constraints missing required fields: $missing"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check ID pattern
  local bad_ids
  bad_ids=$(jq -r '[.constraints[] | select(.id | test("^C-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3}$") | not) | .id] | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_ids" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid constraint IDs: $bad_ids"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check category enum
  local bad_cats
  bad_cats=$(jq -r '
    ["process","git_safety","beads","danger_level","flatline","guardrails","phase_sequencing","eval","bridge","merge","agent_teams","permission"] as $valid |
    [.constraints[] | select(.category | IN($valid[]) | not) | "\(.id): \(.category)"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_cats" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid categories: $bad_cats"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check rule_type enum
  local bad_types
  bad_types=$(jq -r '
    ["NEVER","ALWAYS","WHEN","MUST","SHOULD","MAY"] as $valid |
    [.constraints[] | select(.rule_type | IN($valid[]) | not) | "\(.id): \(.rule_type)"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_types" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid rule_types: $bad_types"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  if [[ "$errors" -eq 0 ]]; then
    pass "Schema validation passed (jq fallback)"
  fi
  return $((errors > 0 ? 1 : 0))
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 3: No duplicate IDs
# ============================================================================

check_unique_ids() {
  log "Check 3: No duplicate IDs"

  local dupes
  dupes=$(jq -r '[.constraints[].id] | sort | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1)) | map(.[0]) | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$dupes" ]]; then
    fail "Duplicate constraint IDs: $dupes"
    return 1
  fi

  pass "All constraint IDs are unique"
  return 0
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 4: Error code cross-references valid
# ============================================================================

check_error_code_refs() {
  log "Check 4: Error code cross-references"

  local error_codes_file=".claude/data/error-codes.json"
  if [[ ! -f "$error_codes_file" ]]; then
    warn "Error codes file not found: $error_codes_file (skipping cross-reference check)"
    return 0
  fi

# ============================================================================

check_layer_coverage() {
  log "Check 5: Layer coverage"

  local no_layers
  no_layers=$(jq -r '[.constraints[] | select((.layers | length) == 0) | .id] | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$no_layers" ]]; then
    fail "Constraints with no layer targets: $no_layers"
    return 1
  fi

  pass "All constraints have ≥1 layer target"
  return 0
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 6: Layer target files exist
# ============================================================================

check_target_files_exist() {
  log "Check 6: Target files exist"

  local errors=0

  # Check protocol files
  local protocol_files
  protocol_files=$(jq -r '[.constraints[].layers[] | select(.target == "protocol") | .file] | unique | .[]' "$REGISTRY")
  while IFS= read -r file; do
    [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
    if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
      fail "Protocol file not found: $file"
      errors=$((errors + 1))

  local -A checked_files
  for entry in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do

    if [[ -z "${checked_files[$s_target]:-}" ]]; then

        fail "Target file not found: $s_target"
        errors=$((errors + 1))
      else
        verbose "Target file exists: $s_target"
      fi
    fi
  done

  if [[ "$errors" -eq 0 ]]; then
    pass "All target files exist"
  fi
  return $((errors > 0 ? 1 : 0))
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 7: Skill names match directories
# ============================================================================

check_skill_names() {
  log "Check 7: Skill names match directories"

  local errors=0

  local skill_names
  skill_names=$(jq -r '[.constraints[].layers[] | select(.target == "skill-md") | .skills[]?] | unique | .[]' "$REGISTRY")

  while IFS= read -r skill; do
    [[ -z "$skill" ]] && continue
    if [[ ! -d ".claude/skills/$skill" ]]; then
      fail "Skill directory not found: .claude/skills/$skill"
      errors=$((errors + 1))
    else
      verbose "Skill directory exists: .claude/skills/$skill"
    fi
  done <<< "$skill_names"

  if [[ "$errors" -eq 0 ]]; then
    pass "All skill names match directories"
  fi
  return $((errors > 0 ? 1 : 0))
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 8: Generated sections are fresh (hash comparison)
# ============================================================================

check_section_freshness() {
  log "Check 8: Section freshness"

  local stale=0

  for entry in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do
    local s_name s_target s_template s_filter
    IFS='|' read -r s_name s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$entry"

    if [[ ! -f "$s_target" ]]; then
      verbose "Skipping freshness for $s_name: target not found"
      continue
    fi

    # Check if markers exist in target
    if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${s_name}" "$s_target" 2>/dev/null; then
      verbose "Skipping freshness for $s_name: no markers in $s_target"
      continue
    fi

    # Extract stored hash from start marker
    local stored_hash
    stored_hash=$(grep "@constraint-generated: start ${s_name}" "$s_target" | sed -n 's/.*hash:\([a-f0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)

    if [[ -z "$stored_hash" ]]; then
      warn "No hash found in marker for section '$s_name' in $s_target"
      continue
    fi

    # Regenerate content
    local template_file="${TEMPLATE_DIR}/${s_template}"
    if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
      fail "Template not found: $template_file"
      stale=$((stale + 1))
      continue
    fi

    local expected_content
    expected_content=$(jq -r "$s_filter" "$REGISTRY" | jq -r -f "$template_file")

    local expected_hash
    expected_hash=$(compute_section_hash "$expected_content")

    if [[ "$stored_hash" != "$expected_hash" ]]; then
      fail "STALE: Section '$s_name' in $s_target (stored: $stored_hash, expected: $expected_hash)"
      stale=$((stale + 1))
    else
      pass "Section '$s_name' in $s_target is fresh"
    fi
  done

  return $((stale > 0 ? 1 : 0))
}

check_orphan_markers() {
  log "Checking for orphan markers"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
     3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
     4	# DEC-0141).
     5	#
     6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
     7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
     8	# PER TASK:
     9	#
    10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
    11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
    12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
    13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
    14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
    15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
    16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
    17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
    18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
    19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
    20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
    21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
    22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
    23	#
    24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
    25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
    26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
    27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
    28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
    29	#
    30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
    31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
    32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
    33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
    34	# file is not written through.
    35	#
    36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
    37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
    38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
    39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
    40	#
    41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
    42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
    43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
    44	# full each time and those caches are gone.
    45	
    46	set -uo pipefail
    47	umask 077
    48	export LC_ALL=C
    49	
    50	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    51	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
    52	[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
    53	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
    54	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
    55	DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
    56	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
    57	DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
    58	STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
    59	SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
    60	LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
    61	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
    62	CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
    63	KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
    64	[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20
    65	
    66	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    67	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    68	[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0
    69	
    70	# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
    71	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    72	source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    73	if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
    74	switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
    75	case "$switch" in
    76	    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
    77	esac
    78	THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
    79	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
    80	THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))
    81	
    82	# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
    83	payload="$(cat)"
    84	[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
    85	fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    86	    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    87	    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
    88	            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
    89	            else 1 end;
    90	    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    91	    select(type == "object") |
    92	    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    93	    ([($tn | tojson),
    94	      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
    95	       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
    96	       else 0 end | tostring),
    97	      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
    98	      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
    99	      (now | todate)] | .[])
   100	' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
   101	{
   102	    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
   103	    IFS= read -r LINES
   104	    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
   105	    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
   106	    IFS= read -r TS
   107	} <<< "$fields"
   108	case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
   109	    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
   110	    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
   111	    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
   112	    *) exit 0 ;;
   113	esac
   114	[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
   115	[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0
   116	
   117	# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
   118	_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
   119	    local s
   120	    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
   121	    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
   122	    printf '%s' "$s"
   123	}
   124	payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
   125	SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   126	[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
   127	SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
   128	
   129	task_raw=""
   130	if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
   131	    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
   132	        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
   133	                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
   134	        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
   135	fi
   136	KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
   137	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
   138	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
   139	
   140	# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
   141	if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
   142	    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
   143	    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
   144	        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
   145	                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
   146	    fi
   147	fi
   148	
   149	# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
   150	[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
   151	[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   152	TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
   153	[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
   154	
   155	PRIOR=0
   156	if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
   157	    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
   158	    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
   159	    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
   160	fi
   161	RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
   162	
   163	printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
   164	    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   165	
   166	# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
   167	# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
   168	n=0
   169	while IFS= read -r old; do
   170	    n=$((n + 1))
   171	    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
   172	        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
   173	    fi
   174	done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)
   175	
   176	# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
   177	OVER=false
   178	(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
   179	sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
   180	[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
   181	if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
   182	    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
   183	    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
   184	            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   185	        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   186	    else
   187	        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   188	    fi
   189	fi
   190	
   191	# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
   192	if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
   193	    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2
   194	
   195	    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
   196	        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
   197	        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
   198	        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
   199	    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
   200	    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
   201	    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
   202	    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   203	    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
   204	        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
   205	        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   206	fi
   207	
   208	exit 0

.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
   118	    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
   119	    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
   120	    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
   122	    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
   123	    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
   124	    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
   125	    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
   126	    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
   127	    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
   128	    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
   129	     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
   130	     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
   131	    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
   132	    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
   133	        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
   134	        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
   135	        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
   136	        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
   137	        else . end)) as $knobs |
   138	    {
   139	      schema_version: 1,
   140	      id: $id,
   141	      profile: $sel.name,
   142	      profile_source: $sel.source,
   143	      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
   144	      profile_keys: $keys,
   145	      knobs: $knobs,
   146	      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
   147	                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
   148	                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
   149	      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
   150	                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# guardrails-orchestrator.sh - Coordinate all guardrail checks
# =============================================================================
# Version: 1.0.0
# Part of: Input Guardrails & Tool Risk Enforcement v1.20.0
#
# Usage:
#   guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
#   guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill deploying-infrastructure --input "Deploy to prod" --mode autonomous
#   guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill implementing-tasks --file input.txt --allow-high
#
# Output: JSON with final action and all check results
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$0")"
readonly PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
readonly CONFIG_FILE="$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"

# Source cross-platform time utilities
# shellcheck source=time-lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/time-lib.sh"

# Scripts
readonly PII_FILTER="$SCRIPT_DIR/pii-filter.sh"
readonly INJECTION_DETECT="$SCRIPT_DIR/injection-detect.sh"
readonly DANGER_LEVEL="$SCRIPT_DIR/danger-level-enforcer.sh"
readonly GUARDRAIL_LOGGER="$SCRIPT_DIR/guardrail-logger.sh"

# Defaults
DEFAULT_MODE="interactive"

# =============================================================================
# Functions
# =============================================================================

show_help() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME [OPTIONS]

Orchestrate all guardrail checks for a skill invocation.

Required Options:
  --skill NAME      Skill identifier
  --input TEXT      Input text to validate (or use --file)
  --file PATH       Read input from file

Optional:
  --mode MODE       Execution mode: interactive (default) or autonomous
  --allow-high      Allow high-risk skills in autonomous mode
  --session-id ID   Session ID for trajectory correlation
  --no-log          Skip trajectory logging
  --parallel NAME   Run specific check in parallel mode
  -h, --help        Show this help message

Guardrail Checks (in order):
  1. danger_level    - Check skill risk level against mode
  2. pii_filter      - Detect and redact sensitive data (blocking)
  3. injection       - Detect prompt injection patterns (blocking)

Output (JSON):
  {
    "action": "PROCEED|WARN|BLOCK",
    "skill": "skill-name",
    "mode": "interactive|autonomous",
    "checks": [...],
    "redacted_input": "sanitized text",
    "latency_ms": N
  }

Examples:
  $SCRIPT_NAME --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
  $SCRIPT_NAME --skill deploying-infrastructure --input "Deploy" --mode autonomous
  $SCRIPT_NAME --skill implementing-tasks --file task.txt --allow-high
EOF
}

# Read config value with default
get_config() {
    local key="$1"
    local default="$2"

    if [[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
        local value
        value=$(yq -r "$key // \"$default\"" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "$default")
        if [[ "$value" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "$default"
        else
            echo "$value"
        fi
    else
        echo "$default"
    fi
}

# Check if guardrails are enabled: the explicit key, else the loa.profile
# default (cycle-129 D-9.1; `standard` reads false). get_config's `// default`
# would read an explicit false as the default.
# shellcheck source=lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"
is_enabled() {
    local enabled
    enabled=$(loa_knob guardrails.input.enabled false)
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]]
}

# Check if specific guardrail is enabled
is_check_enabled() {
    local check="$1"
    local enabled
    enabled=$(get_config ".guardrails.input.${check}.enabled" "true")
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]]
}

# Get check mode (blocking/parallel/advisory)
get_check_mode() {
    local check="$1"
    get_config ".guardrails.input.${check}.mode" "blocking"
}

# Get injection threshold
get_injection_threshold() {
    get_config ".guardrails.input.injection_detection.threshold" "0.7"
}

# Run PII filter
run_pii_filter() {
    local input="$1"

    if ! is_check_enabled "pii_filter"; then
        echo '{"name":"pii_filter","status":"SKIP","mode":"disabled"}'
        return
    fi

# Run injection detection
run_injection_detection() {
    local input="$1"

    if ! is_check_enabled "injection_detection"; then
        echo '{"name":"injection_detection","status":"SKIP","mode":"disabled"}'
        return
    fi

    local mode
    mode=$(get_check_mode "injection_detection")
    local threshold
    threshold=$(get_injection_threshold)

    local result
    result=$("$INJECTION_DETECT" --input "$input" --threshold "$threshold" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"status":"ERROR","score":0}')

    local status
    status=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.status')
    local score
    score=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.score')
    local patterns
    patterns=$(echo "$result" | jq -c '.patterns_matched')
    local latency
    latency=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.latency_ms')

    # Map DETECTED -> FAIL for blocking mode
    if [[ "$status" == "DETECTED" && "$mode" == "blocking" ]]; then
        status="FAIL"
    fi

    cat <<EOF
{
  "name": "injection_detection",
  "status": "$status",
  "mode": "$mode",
  "score": $score,
  "threshold": $threshold,
  "patterns_matched": $patterns,
  "latency_ms": $latency
}
EOF
}

# Run danger level check
run_danger_level() {
    local skill="$1"
    local mode="$2"
    local allow_high="$3"

    local args=("--skill" "$skill" "--mode" "$mode")
    if [[ "$allow_high" == "true" ]]; then
        args+=("--allow-high")
    fi

    local result
    result=$("$DANGER_LEVEL" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"action":"BLOCK","reason":"error"}')

    local action
    action=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.action')
    local level
    level=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.level')
    local reason
    reason=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.reason')

    # Map to status
    local status="PASS"
    if [[ "$action" == "BLOCK" ]]; then
        status="FAIL"
    elif [[ "$action" == "WARN" ]]; then
        status="WARN"
    fi

    cat <<EOF
{
  "name": "danger_level",
  "status": "$status",
  "level": "$level",
  "mode": "$mode",
  "reason": "$reason"
}
EOF
}

# Determine final action from all checks
determine_final_action() {
    local checks="$1"

    # Check for any FAIL status
    local has_fail
    has_fail=$(echo "$checks" | jq '[.[] | select(.status == "FAIL")] | length')
    if [[ "$has_fail" -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo "BLOCK"
        return
    fi

    # Check for any WARN status
    local has_warn
    has_warn=$(echo "$checks" | jq '[.[] | select(.status == "WARN")] | length')
    if [[ "$has_warn" -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo "WARN"
        return
    fi

    echo "PROCEED"
}

# Get blocking reason from failed checks
get_block_reason() {
    local checks="$1"

    local failed
    failed=$(echo "$checks" | jq -r '[.[] | select(.status == "FAIL")] | .[0].name // "unknown"')

    case "$failed" in
        danger_level)
            echo "$checks" | jq -r '[.[] | select(.name == "danger_level")] | .[0].reason'
            ;;
        injection_detection)
            echo "Prompt injection detected"
            ;;
        pii_filter)
            echo "PII filter blocked input"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Guardrail check failed"
            ;;
    esac
}

# =============================================================================
# Main
# =============================================================================

main() {
    local skill=""
    local input=""
    local mode="$DEFAULT_MODE"
    local allow_high="false"
    local session_id="${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-}"
    local do_log="true"
    local start_time

    start_time=$(get_timestamp_ms)

    # Parse arguments
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --skill)
                skill="$2"
                shift 2
                ;;
            --input)
                input="$2"
                shift 2
                ;;
            --file)
                if [[ ! -f "$2" ]]; then
                    echo "Error: File not found: $2" >&2
                    exit 1
                fi
                input=$(cat "$2")
                shift 2
                ;;
            --mode)
                mode="$2"
                shift 2
                ;;
            --allow-high)
                allow_high="true"
                shift
                ;;
            --session-id)
                session_id="$2"
                shift 2
                ;;
            --no-log)
                do_log="false"
                shift
                ;;
            --parallel)
                # For future parallel mode support
                shift 2
                ;;
            -h|--help)
                show_help
                exit 0
                ;;
            *)
                echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2
                show_help
                exit 1
                ;;
        esac
    done

    # Validate required arguments
    if [[ -z "$skill" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --skill is required" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    if [[ -z "$input" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --input or --file is required" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    # Check if guardrails are enabled
    if ! is_enabled; then
        cat <<EOF
{
  "action": "PROCEED",
  "skill": "$skill",
  "mode": "$mode",
  "checks": [],
  "reason": "guardrails disabled in config",
  "latency_ms": 0
}
EOF
        exit 0
    fi

    # Run all checks
    local checks=()
    local redacted_input="$input"

    # 1. Danger level check
    local danger_result
    danger_result=$(run_danger_level "$skill" "$mode" "$allow_high")
    checks+=("$danger_result")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/guard-yield.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.2 … AC-1.4,
# SDD D-1.3, D-1.4)
# guard-yield.sh over a fixture audit log and a rotated segment, at a fixed
# --now: replay exclusion (flag, cwd, burst) counted in the header, the
# likely-false-positive heuristic (heredoc, outside-repo cwd, prose class without
# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the
# --check drift gate (0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit, 0 after a
# yield-only change), the --json shape, and no command text or cwd in any output.
# =============================================================================

NOW="2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"

setup() {
  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gyield.XXXXXX")"
  T="$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)"
  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/scratch"
  # A temp prefix the fixture controls (the script's own mktemp also uses it).
  export TMPDIR="$T"
  cp "$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml" "$T/origins.yaml"
  cp "$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md" "$T/hooks-reference.md"
  A="$T/audit.jsonl"
  row() {  # ts pattern cwd command [extra-json]
    jq -cn --arg ts "$1" --arg p "$2" --arg cwd "$3" --arg c "$4" --argjson x "${5:-{\}}" \
      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $c, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: "claude-test-model", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $p, matched: "m"} + $x'
  }
  {
    # live, inside the repo
    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"$'\n'"hello"$'\n'"EOF"   # complete non-executing heredoc → likely FP (FR-6 classifier via lib/heredoc-classifier.sh)
    row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP
    row "2026-10-12T10:00:00Z" "SP-1" "$ROOT" "br comments add bd-1 'note about spike/x merge'" # prose class, no verb → likely FP
    row "2026-10-13T23:59:00Z" "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS" "$ROOT" "cd sub && rm -rf ./.cache"             # prose class WITH verb → real
    # replays
    row "2026-10-11T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~1" '{"replay": true}'        # flag
    row "2026-10-11T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$T/scratch" "git reset --hard HEAD~2"                       # cwd under TMPDIR
    row "2026-10-11T10:00:00Z" "P3" "/home/u/bats-run-42/repo" "git reset --hard HEAD~3"        # cwd /bats-run-
    for s in 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09; do                                                  # burst: 10 in one minute
      row "2026-10-09T10:00:${s}Z" "P2" "$ROOT" "git push --force origin main"
    done
    # outside the window
    row "2026-08-01T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~9"
    # implement-gate telemetry and ask
    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:00:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "telemetry", cwd: "x"}'
    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:05:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "ask", cwd: "x"}'
    # a non-block row and an unparseable line
    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:10:00Z", tool: "Bash", command: "ls", cwd: "x"}'
    printf 'this is not json\n'
  } > "$A"
  # the rotated segment holds the one real P3 catch
  row "2026-10-10T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~3" > "$A.1"
  ARGS=(--now "$NOW" --audit-log "$A" --origins "$T/origins.yaml" --out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --hooks-ref "$T/hooks-reference.md")
}
teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

g() { jq -c --arg id "$1" '.guards[] | select(.id == $id) | [.blocks_30d, .likely_fp_30d, .telemetry_30d, .last_real_catch]' "$T/run/guard-yield.json"; }

@test "GY-1 replay rows are excluded by flag, cwd and burst and counted in the header; the window and bad rows are honoured" {
  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"

  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_unparseable' "$J")" = "1" ]
  [ "$(jq -c '.totals | [.blocks_30d, .real_blocks_30d, .likely_fp_30d, .telemetry_30d]' "$J")" = '[5,2,3,2]' ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.scope' "$J")" = "host" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.window_days' "$J")" = "30" ]
}

@test "GY-2 the rotated segment is read: its real P3 catch is counted and is the guard's last_real_catch" {
  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(g fence:P3)" = '[1,0,0,"2026-10-10"]' ]
}

+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]

+@test "IG-11 the example documents implement_gate: the three modes, the claims modifier, the sanction paths and the override; the default is ask (cycle-129 D-4.1 supersedes the cycle-126 'undocumented' pin)" {

+# =============================================================================
+# cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.1 (SDD D-4.1, PRD AC-4.1): the mode matrix
+# mode {unset, ask, telemetry, deny} × claims {plain, authoritative} × write {app, trust}
+# × sanction {none, run_fresh, run_stale, marker_fresh, marker_stale, override}
+# × cache {fresh, stale, missing, unparseable} (run_* sanctions define the cache themselves)
+# =============================================================================
+
+# $1 mode (unset = no key) $2 claims (plain | authoritative)
+cfg_gate() {
+    : > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    if [[ "$1" != unset || "$2" == authoritative ]]; then
+        printf 'implement_gate:\n' >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ "$1" != unset ]] && printf '  mode: %s\n' "$1" >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ "$2" == authoritative ]] && printf '  claims: authoritative\n' >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    fi
+    return 0
+}
+
+# $1 cache: fresh | stale | missing | unparseable | run_fresh | run_stale (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    case "$1" in
+        missing) ;;
+        unparseable) printf '{"state": "RUNNING", \n' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        fresh)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        stale)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_fresh) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_stale) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# $1 sanction: none | marker_fresh | marker_stale | override (run_* handled by cache_state); echoes the override value
+marker_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json"
+    case "$1" in
+        marker_fresh) jq -nc '{skill: "implement", sprint: "sprint-256", started_at: (now | floor | todate)}' > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json" ;;

+    esac

+# $1 path $2 claims $3 override (1 or empty) — stdout/stderr split, LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1

## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill {{SKILL}} --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the
active skill is continuous-learning itself.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
     4	# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
     5	#
     6	# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
     7	# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
     8	# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
     9	# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
    10	# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
    11	# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    19	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    20	    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    21	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    22	    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    23	    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    24	    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    25	    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    26	    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    27	    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    28	    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    29	    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    30	    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    31	    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    32	    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    33	    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    34	    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
    35	}
    36	
    37	# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
    38	checkpoint() {
    39	    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
    40	        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
    41	          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
    42	        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    43	}
    44	
    45	# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
    46	write_lines() {
    47	    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    48	    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    49	    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
    50	        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
    51	        | bash "$HOOK"
    52	}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  [[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

check_constraint_blocks() {
  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "CLAUDE.loa.md not found"
    return
  fi

  local block_count
  block_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$block_count" ]] && block_count=0

  if [[ "$block_count" -ge 3 ]]; then
    report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "$block_count constraint-generated blocks found"
  elif [[ "$block_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraint-blocks" "Only $block_count constraint-generated blocks (expected 3+)"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "No constraint-generated blocks found"
  fi

  # Check start/end pairs match
  local start_count end_count
  start_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  end_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: end' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$start_count" ]] && start_count=0
  [[ -z "$end_count" ]] && end_count=0

  if [[ "$start_count" -ne "$end_count" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "Mismatched start/end pairs: $start_count starts, $end_count ends"
  fi
}

7. Create/checkout the feature branch via `.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh ensure-branch "$target"`.

All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."
